Laṅkākāṇḍa
(‘book or section dealing with लङ्का’)
------------------------------------------
The Rāmcaritamānasa of गोस्वामी Tulasīdās (A.

-1623) written in the Avadhī dialect of the Hindi language is the most celebrated version of the Rāmāyaṇa, highly venerated in the Hindi belt of North India. It is based more on the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa than on that of वाल्मीकि.
Out of the seven kāṇḍas or books of this work, the sixth has been named by him as the Laṅkākāṇḍa instead of Yuddhakāṇḍa as done by वाल्मीकि. The content is the same except for some minor variations.
See RĀMCARITAMĀNASA and TULASĪDĀS.

Laṅkā
------------------------------------------
Laṅkā has been well-known to the students of Hindu म्य्थोलोग्य् as the capital of the demon king रावण. The original builder of this city was Māli. He had got it built by the divine architect विश्वकर्म and was living there along with his brothers Mālyavān and Sukeśa.
Since Māli had become a terror to the gods, विष्णु killed him. When the demons deserted the city and took refuge in पाताल or the nether world, it was given to कुबेर the king of the yakṣas (a type of demigods). रावण, a cousin of कुबेर, drove him away and occupied it. He started ruling it assisted by his brothers Kumbha-कर्ण and विभीषण as also his eldest son मेघनाद or इन्द्रजित्.
Laṅkā was a very rich and prosperous city of dazzling splendour. Its citizens, the rākṣasa tribes, were physically strong but ruthless in nature. They were addicted to sense-pleasures and drinking. Even cannibalism was not uncommon among them. Laṅkiṇī was the demon-protectress of the city.
When हनुमान् vanquished her she disappeared from the scene saying that her time was over and the city would soon be destroyed.
See also RĀMĀYAṆA.
